 Judgment

Married daughters of Yashodamma filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW- 8543 alleging that on 13.12.2023 at 5.30 p.m., when Yashodamma was traveling by sitting on the pillion of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 rode by her son Naveen Kumar-respondent No.1 from Seegehalli towards Hasigala village, near Hunasenahalli villge, Shidlaghatta taluk, respondent No.1 rode the Motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, unable to observe pothole, unable to control Motorcycle, fell along with Motorcycle and pillion rider, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous head injury to Yashodamma. Immediately after accident, Yashodamma has been shifted to Govt. Hospital,
Siddlaghatta, wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to NIMHANS hospita, then shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein on 14.12.2023 Yashodamma succumbed to the injuries.
2. Regarding accident Shiddlaghatta police registered a case in crime No.309/2023 against respondent No.1.
3.

As on the date of accident, deceased Yashodamma being aged 56 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/-
p.m. by working as Coolie and used to contribute entire income to the family.
4. Inspite of service of notice to respondent No.1- owner/rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2- Insurance company appeared through his advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident, age,
occupation and income of the deceased Yashodamma.
Respondent No.2-Insurance company denied liability to indemnify respondent No.1 on the ground that respondent No.1 violated driver clause of the policy.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 06.12.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 13.12.2023 at about 05.30 p.m., on Seegehalli - Hasigala road, near Hunasenahalli village, Siddlaghatta taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EW- Vanajakshi vs Naveen Kumar H D on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40131643/
2 8543, by respondent No.1 H.D.Naveen Kumar, Motorcycle fell, thereby accident taken place resulting in the head injury to Smt.Yashodamma, W/o.Devaraju, pillion rider, who succumbed to injuries on 14.12.2023?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. On 09.04.2025 petitioner No.2-Rupa deposed as P.W.1 and produced 9 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.9.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.12,73,036/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondent No.1 as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1:- In the evidence P.W.1 stated that on 13.12.2023 at 5.30 p.m., when her mother - Yashodamma was traveling by sitting on the pillion of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 rode by respondent No.1-Naveen Kumar from Seegehalli towards Hasigala village, near Hunasenahalli villge, Shidlaghatta taluk, respondent No.1 negligently rode the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543, unable to observe pothole, unable to control Motorcycle, fell along with Motorcycle and pillion rider, thereby caused the accident, caused head injuries to Yashodamma.
11.

P.W.1 stated that, immediately after accident, Yashodamma has been shifted to Govt. Hospital,
Shiddlaghatta, wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to NIMHANS hospital, then admitted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein on 14.12.2023 Yashodamma succumbed to the injuries.
12. In the written statement, respondent No.2- Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
13. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted that she never witnessed the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.309/2023 registered by Siddlaghatta Rural police on 14.12.2023 at 7.30 hours against respondent No.1, the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC, on the basis of the complaint presented by Manjunatha M., S/o.Munikempanna.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of Sketch of place of accident.

Ex.P.4 is the Vanajakshi vs Naveen Kumar H D on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40131643/
3 Motor vehicles Accident Report.

sentences.text: Ex.P.5 is the copy of Inquest Mahazar with enclosures.

15. Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet filed by Shiddlaghatta Rural police in crime No.309/2023 against the respondent No.1-Naveen Kumar, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304-A of IPC and Section 3, 181 of IMV Act.
16. In the police records, name of Yashodamma is noted as pillion rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW- 8543 and victim of the accident.
17. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

18. Hence, I have concluded that on 13.12.2023 at 5.30 p.m., when Yashodamma was traveling by sitting on the pillion of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 rode by respondent No.1-Naveen Kumar from Seegehalli towards Hasigala village, near Hunasenahalli village, Shidlaghatta taluk,
respondent No.1-Naveen Kumar rode the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 negligently without observing pothole, unable to control Motorcycle, fell along with Motorcycle and pillion rider, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to pillion rider-Yashodamma, who succumbed to those injuries on 14.12.2023 at Victoria hospital.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

In the affidavit evidence P.W.1-Rupa stated that as on the date of accident her mother Yashodamma being aged about 56 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by preparing condiment items and distributing to small shops and used to contribute entire income to the family.
20. In the written statement respondent No.2 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of deceased Yashodhamma.

21. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of incident, her mother being aged more than 60 years neither having independent source of income nor earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
P.W.1 admitted that her mother Yashodhamma resided with her son - respondent No.1 - Naveen Kumar. .
22. In the P.M.Report and Inquest Mahazar, age of Yashodamma is noted as 56 years as on the date of accident.
In the copy of the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.8 date of birth of Yashodamma is noted as 01.01.1967.
Aadhar cards shows that petitioners are the daughters of Yashodhamma.
23. In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of deceased Yashodhamma.
To the daughters, mother is always mother irrespective of marriage and residing with the spouses.

Hence, I have calculated the compensation under the head of loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of incident, deceased Yashodhamma being aged about 57 years, used to earn Rs.16,000/- p.m. and used to contribute 2/3rd of her income to the petitioners-daughters and by Vanajakshi vs Naveen Kumar H D on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40131643/
4 applying multiplier '9', in the following terms:
Age of deceased Yashodamma as on the 57 years date of incident - Notional monthly income of the deceased Rs.16,000/- as on the date of incident - Less : 1/3rd deduction towards personal Rs.10,667/-
 expenses of the deceased (16,000 -  5,333= 10,667)
 Annual income of the deceased (10,667 x 12) Rs.1,28,004/-
 Loss of dependency Rs.1,28,004/- x 9 Rs.11,52,036/-
24. Hence, I award compensation of Rs.11,52,036/-
under the head loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/- towards consortium to petitioner No.1 & 2 at the rate of Rs.44,000/-
each.
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1. Loss of dependency 11,52,036-00 2. Loss of estate 16,500-00 3.
Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00 petitioners (44,000/- x 2) Total 12,73,036-00 25.

As petitioners have not produced documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of Yashodamma, no money is added towards the future prospects while calculating the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

26. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being the daughters of Yashodamma are entitle to receive Rs.12,73,036/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation.

27. In the written statement, respondent No.2 Insurance Company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 as on the date of incident, however,

5 denied liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 on the ground that Naveen Kumar owner/insured of the Motorcycle has violated the driver clause of the policy.

sentences.text:
Copy of the charge sheet shows that,
after investigation police have filed charge sheet alleging that respondent No.1 - Naveen Kumar has committed offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC and Section 3 r/w. Sec.181 of IMV Act, i.e. by driving the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 without license.
In the file there are no documents to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.1 - Naveen Kumar had license to ride Motorcycle with gear.

Hence, I have concluded that as respondent No.1 who violated the driver clause of the policy is not entitle to be indemnified by the respondent No.2 - Insurance company and he is alone liable to pay compensation to his sisters (petitioners) and an award is to be passed directing the respondent No.1 to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 being the owner/rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EW-8543 shall pay Rs.12,73,036/- (Rupees Twelve lakhs Seventy Three thousand thirty six only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 6 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners may be released by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 3rd day of May, 2025.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
